kpis.name: Novartis partnership for votoplam HD
kpis.explanation: Collaboration agreement with Novartis for development and commercialization of the votoplam program
kpis.description: In November 2024, PTC Therapeutics established a partnership with Novartis for the votoplam HD program including associated molecules. PTC received 1 billion dollars upfront in January 2025 and can receive up to 1.9 billion dollars in development, regulatory, and sales milestones, 40% profit share in the United States, and double-digit royalties outside the United States
kpis.signal: Strategic partnership validating technology and generating substantial revenues

kpis.name: Sephience regulatory approvals
kpis.explanation: Series of regulatory approvals obtained for Sephience (sepiapterin) in multiple regions
kpis.description: Sephience (sepiapterin) obtained major regulatory approvals: June 2025 European Union, July 2025 United States (FDA), December 2025 Japan. These approvals mark a significant commercial milestone for phenylketonuria treatment. PTC paid 57.5 million dollars in regulatory and development milestones in 2025
kpis.signal: Worldwide regulatory validation of Sephience for PKU treatment

risks.title: Loss of Translarna revenues in Europe
risks.score_rationale: Central position in 10-K with mention of substantial risk to revenues. Strong language: 'substantial risk' of revenue loss. Context aggravated by withdrawal of marketing authorization in EEA. Regulatory category heavily weighted.

risks.title: Failure of Translarna development in United States
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of withdrawal of MAA request following regulatory failure. Definitive language: 'further development not planned'. Major impact on strategy. Critical Regulatory category.

risks.title: Generic competition on Emflaza
risks.score_rationale: Documented risk with loss of exclusivity in 2024 and confirmed negative impact on revenues. Clear language on future impact. Moderate weight Competition category.

risks.title: Failure of vatiquinone MAA for FA
risks.score_rationale: Complete response letter from FDA requiring new study. Strong language: 'substantial evidence not demonstrated'. High risk for advanced-stage product. Regulatory category.

risks.title: Dependence on pricing recognition
risks.score_rationale: Repeated mention of country-by-country negotiations for Sephience. Direct risk to commercial launch. Language underscoring regulatory vulnerability. Regulatory category.

risks.title: Dependence on external partnerships
risks.score_rationale: References to agreements with Roche and Novartis. Partial loss of control over development (ex. votoplam). Cautious but not urgent language. Moderate Capital category.

risks.title: Risk on post-Authorization studies
risks.score_rationale: Post-commercialization obligations for Kebilidi mentioned. Standard language on regulatory requirements. Less critical than other regulatory risks. Regulatory category.

ai_positioning.summary: PTC Therapeutics, Inc. does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report. The information provided focuses on financial aspects, products, and collaborations, with no reference to AI.
